facts.Foundshore Verdict: Strong fit for eligible Berkeley founders.
facts.Funding / Support: US$50K stipend per founding team + up to US$350K Azure credits + NVIDIA Inception + up to US$25K Orrick legal credits + SkyDeck Pad-13 access
facts.Equity / Economic Terms: Stipend described without published equity take on current Mayfield page
facts.Geography / Affiliation Restriction: Current UC Berkeley student or alumni ≤3 years post-graduation
facts.Official / Must-Have Requirements: Current UC Berkeley students or alumni within three years of graduation, focused on AI at inception.
facts.Strong-to-Have: Technical founders with an AI problem thesis or prototype and the ability to use Azure, NVIDIA and SkyDeck resources.
facts.On-site / Attendance: A Berkeley ecosystem program; check the current application page for in-person arrangements.
facts.International Founder: Yes if Berkeley affiliation and US participation requirements are met
facts.Visa / Relocation: No separate visa sponsorship announcement; Berkeley affiliation is the main eligibility restriction.
facts.Deadline / Next Intake: 2026 cohort announced; next application window recheck
facts.Application Materials: Official Mayfield AI Garage application; founder/team and AI company concept.
facts.Foundshore Best Fit: Current UC Berkeley students or alumni who graduated within three years, building AI at inception. Early cash, compute, legal and SkyDeck support may suit teams without substantial traction.
facts.Foundshore Not Fit: Applicants without Berkeley affiliation, non-AI projects, mature companies or those seeking a traditional curriculum rather than inception-stage support.
facts.Notes: A focused opportunity for AI builders with a qualifying Berkeley affiliation, not a broadly eligible international-founder program.
